episodes.169099: Several pulse thunderstorms produced sporadic wind damage.
episodes.169100: Several pulse thunderstorms produced sporadic wind damage.
episodes.169173: As a cold front moved south into the region, the airmass ahead of this was warm and unstable. Storms developed along and ahead of the front and especially from intersecting outflow boundaries and storm mergers. This resulted in some being severe and causing wind damage. Trees and power lines were blown down, but a tornado did occur and cause some structural damage.
episodes.169290: As an area of high pressure remained centered east of New Mexico, deep monsoonal moisture continued to surge into northern and central New Mexico on June 26, 2022. An embedded easterly wave helped in the development and intensification of numerous thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours. Northeast Roswell was hit hardest as thunderstorms with heavy rainfall rates caused flash flooding across portions of the city. A blocked drainage gate was responsible for flooding at least a dozen homes in the Holly Loop subdivision, and elsewhere in Roswell, an overflowing Borrendo Creek caused a bridge to collapse.
episodes.169549: Afternoon thunderstorms produce street flooding near Bradenton in Manatee County.
episodes.169551: Afternoon thunderstorms produce waterspouts and gusty marine winds across coastal waters.
episodes.169635: Sufficient moisture combined with daytime heating resulted in moderate instability, especially across southwest Arizona with SPC mesoanalysis showing MLCAPE of 1000 J/KG and DCAPE of 2000 J/KG. This resulted in the development of strong to locally severe isolated thunderstorms across portions of Yuma and La Paz counties, with strong downburst winds and dense blowing dust being the main hazards. There was also a popular social media photo of a possible landspout tornado in the Buckeye area. No damages or injuries were reported.
episodes.169645: A cluster of storms from a mesoscale convective system that crossed Kentucky moved southwest into East Tennessee in the evening, producing gusty winds that blew down a few trees in the southern Tennessee Valley.
episodes.169686: A long-lived thunderstorm cluster moved east-southeast during the morning hours across  the mid Mississippi Valley. These storms moved into an axis of greater instability over southeast Missouri, contributing to an uptick in intensity. Wind damage was observed in portions of Wayne and Stoddard Counties. Rather weak wind shear limited the duration and areal extent of the severe storms. A mid-level shortwave trough moved east-southeastward from the upper Mississippi Valley across the Great Lakes. The storms occurred near an associated surface cold front that moved southeastward across the Ohio Valley and southern Missouri.
episodes.169738: A shower just east of Satellite Beach in Brevard County produced a short-lived waterspout.
episodes.169782: A severe storm developed in a line of thunderstorms causing wind damage before moving into southwestern Missouri.
episodes.169785: Thunderstorms developed during the early morning of the 26th when a cold front moved over the area. Several strong to severe storms impacted Hickory, Dallas and Polk counties, mainly producing damaging wind gusts. Rainfall accumulations averaged between one and two inches north of Interstate 44 during the storm event on the 26th.
episodes.169811: A slow-moving cold front traversed the Mid-South on 06/26/2022 producing numerous showers and thunderstorms with isolated large hail and strong wind.
episodes.169813: A slow-moving cold front traversed the Mid-South on 06/26/2022 producing numerous showers and thunderstorms with isolated large hail and strong wind.
episodes.169866: An upper level ridge was centered over Texas. A weak cold front had moved into Southeast New Mexico the previous night. High moisture was across the area. These conditions resulted in a thunderstorm that produced wind damage on the north side of Carlsbad.
episodes.169901: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a weak pre-frontal trough during the early afternoon hours. The very moist dew points in the lower to middle 70s allowed for plenty of instability, but the lack of notable shear prevented storm organization. Instead, the collapse of precipitation-loaded storm cores caused scattered strong wind gusts and isolated instances of marginally severe wind damage.
episodes.170007: Prior to the arrival of a prefrontal trough, some thunderstorms managed to take advantage of limited instability in Central New York in the afternoon of the 26th. One thunderstorm over Chenango County became severe and knocked trees and wires down.
episodes.170193: A cold front triggered bands of strong to severe thunderstorms across west-central Illinois during the evening of June 25th.  Some of the cells produced wind gusts up to 60mph, resulting in scattered wind damage.  In addition, excessive rainfall rates led to localized flash flooding with some of the stronger storms.
episodes.170241: Daytime heating and an abundance of moisture stirred up afternoon showers and thunderstorms across West Virginia from June 25th to the 27th. The first round of convection on the 25th resulted in several trees down around Central West Virginia while flash flooding took center stage on the 26th and 27th. The town of Flatwoods observed flooding of local businesses as a result of Granny Creek rising out of its banks from all the heavy downpours within passing thunderstorms.
episodes.170243: Isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms trekking through eastern Kentucky on the afternoon of June 25th led to heavy downpours and a localized instance of flash flooding. As heavy rain fell down, water seeped into the basement of a home in Olive Hill.
episodes.170244: Heavy downpours accompanying afternoon showers and thunderstorms on June 25th led to one instance of flooding in Dickenson County. High water was observed for a brief period of time at a local intersection, but quickly drained away once the showers and storms came to a close for that day.
episodes.170709: An unstable atmosphere developed during the afternoon and evening hours over northern Alabama and portions of southern middle Tennessee. A few pulse showers/storm developed and intensified and producing some damaging winds in Lincoln county, TN.
episodes.170813: As the dominant upper level ridge began to ease farther off to the west over the Upper Red River Valley on June 26th, a weak upper trough was able to slide south into the region, reinforcing a weak cool front southward. This front encountered a moist and moderately unstable environment as it entered Southwest Arkansas, North Louisiana, and East Texas during the afternoon, with strong forcing yielding the development of scattered showers and thunderstorms across these areas. Some of these storms were severe, producing multiple reports of damaging winds across portions of North-central Louisiana before exiting the region into Central Louisiana during the evening.
episodes.171203: A weak cold front drifted into the region while a series of upper disturbances moved across the region. This produced multiple rounds of mainly afternoon storms, some of which became severe.
episodes.171417: Deep monsoon moisture and slow mid level winds allowed slow moving thunderstorms to produce heavy rain and flash flooding over and below the Pipeline Fire scar. Flash flooding was also seen in Flagstaff.
episodes.171514: Thunderstorms developed in southeast and south central Kansas. There were a couple of storms that produced quarter sized hail during the late evening into the overnight hours.
episodes.171523: Thunderstorms moved southwest across southeast Arizona. Thunderstorm winds produced a wall of dust along I-10 in Pinal County. Other storms produced heavy rain and flash flooding in the Baboquivari Mountains.
episodes.171599: Thunderstorms developed along a pre-frontal trough in the Finger Lakes region and tracked northeast into north central New York. The eastern Lake Ontario region was mostly sunny through the day which allowed for untapped instability as storms were approaching the region. Even with weak shear, storms were able to become semi-organized across Oswego and western Lewis counties with one lone report of wind damage.
episodes.171657: A stalled frontal system near Lake Okeechobee contributed to the development of afternoon showers and thunderstorms across South Florida and the adjacent coastal waters.
episodes.171678: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across the Upper Cumberland during the late afternoon and evening hours on June 25. One storm produced significant wind damage in Overton County.
episodes.171679: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed across Middle Tennessee during the afternoon and evening hours on June 26. A couple of reports of large hail and wind damage were received.
episodes.171841: An increase of monsoonal moisture resulted in multiple storms with microburst wind gusts in northern Utah, as well as flash flooding in portions of southern Utah.

events.narrative: Water entered into the basement of a home in the town of Olive Hill.
High water was observed at the intersection of Coeburn Road and Honey Camp Road.
Sporadic tree damage occurred along Little Eagle Creek Road near Highway 111 northeast of Livingston.

A NWS storm survey determined a west-southwestward moving severe thunderstorm produced a significant 1.5 mile long by 0.75 mile wide microburst across northern Livingston. Damage began on the northeast side of Livingston near School Mountain Road at Highway 111 then continued west-southwestward through the northern side of the city, where multiple trees were uprooted, tin was peeled off the metal roof of a house, and a few trees fell onto vehicles on Kennedy Street and Buena Vista Road. Multiple trees were also uprooted and a couple of trees were snapped along Greenfield Drive and Hillcrest Drive, with one tree falling through a house on Greenfield Drive. Damage totals reached 1.6 million dollars per the Livingston mayor. Winds were estimated up to 70 mph.
A tree was blown down and corn crops were damaged along Ford Road northwest of Grand Prairie.
Several tree branches and power lines were blown down.
Corn crops were flattened and a large dead tree limb was blown down just north of Business 24.
Several tree limbs were blown down, one of which hit a power line and led to a power outage.
Mesonet weather station west northwest of Palm Canyon reported a 59 mph wind gust.
Several streets were flooded in Normal.
A picture was sent via Facebook of 4.1 inches of rain that fell from showers and storms during the overnight into the morning hours.
The South Fork of the Sangamon River spilled out of its banks and flowed across Route 104 just east of Kincaid.
Water was flowing across Davis Road northeast of Pawnee.

As many as 30 large trees and tree tops were reported down between the Pittsburg and Hermitage sides of Pomme De Terre State Park. One pickup truck was heavily damaged from a falling tree. Numerous canopies and popups suffered damage from high winds.
Two very large trees were reported down across Highway H a half mile from Highway 83 in Elkton.
A short path of sporadic tree damage was reported along Highway KK. A few large trees were snapped and a home suffered minor roof and siding damage.
The Mesonet site FW7752 in Pleasant Hope recorded a 63 MPH wind gust.
A power line was reported down at the Old Rock Quarry at the RA and Highway 64 Junction.
Several large limbs were reported down from high winds. Up to an inch of rain also fell in less than an hour.
Numerous trees were reported down or uprooted. A power line was also reported down.
Three large trees and several large limbs were reported down.

High water was observed along Coal City Road near Princewick. Lego Road was also under water for a brief time outside the town of Besoco.
Five to ten trees were blown down across roads in western Wayne County from Piedmont to the Williamsville area.

A power pole was snapped in Puxico. Numerous large branches and a few trees were down from Puxico northeast toward Advance.

Significant wind damage was reported across a good part of northern Stoddard County, including the Advance and Bell City areas. The most significant damage was on Highway 51 right near the Bollinger County line, where several large trees were broken and a half-ton truck and camper were flipped over. Only minor injuries were reported. Elsewhere, a few trees and some large branches were down. A large branch fell on a house a half-mile north of Bell City.
Dispatch reported that thunderstorm winds had blown down a tree onto KY-52 West near Beattyville.
Two people were transported to the hospital after being struck by lightning at a campground.
Tree damage was reported in western Augusta County, including along VA-42 Scenic Highway/Little Calf Pasture Highway, and VA-254 Parkersburg Turnpike.
Twitter tSpotter photo showed a boat dock was flipped over in the Roans Creek area.
Several trees and wires blew down bringing down 3 poles in Lost River.
A NWS employee reported a 3-inch diameter tree limb blown down along Oakwood Drive.

Several trees blew down in Shenandoah County, including along VA-698 Red Banks Road and VA-726 Hepner Road in Mount Jackson. Other minor tree damage was reported on VA-714 Julius Keller Road near VA-606 Gap Road, and on VA-676 Fravel Road near Spring Hollow Road.

Thunderstorms produced one inch of rain in less than one hour over the Contreras burn scar causing a debris flow over State Route 386 to Kitt Peak.

Multiple trees and power lines were downed on Blade Loop Road and Highway 8 in the Whitehall community. Multiple trees and power lines were also downed on Highway 84, and Highway 460 near Hance Road in Whitehall.

Utility company reported flooding near intersection of US Highway 41 and 14th Street West.
A flash flood occurred in Cottonwood and Burro Washes as well as Sheets Gulch. Notom-Bullfrog road was washed out.

A thunderstorm produced wind damage on the north side of Carlsbad. Multiple tree branches were blown down with some as large as six inches in diameter. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
Trees were blown down across Highway 90.
Trees and wires were downed onto Osceola Road.
A barn collapsed at this location and a tree was split as well. Several tree limbs were also knocked down near Barnes Hollow Road off of Pulaski highway.

Over three inches of rain in Roswell caused significant flooding on the northeast side of the city. At least twelve homes in the Holly Loop subdividion were flooded, and emergency crews had to divert water through cinder block walls away from the subdivision and onto East Country Club Road. Farther east, a small bridge collapsed at East Mescalero Road near La Jara Road due to flood waters in Borrendo Creek. Damages are estimated.

Numerous outflow boundaries collided to form a severe thunderstorm. This thunderstorm resulted in multiple trees being blown down in the 1400-1500 block of Midway Road. Power lines were also blown down and two homes sustained roof damage. The roof was also blown off of a chicken house and a tree was blown down across Highway 43 at Mary Crapps Road.
Multiple social media videos showed street flooding across south Bradenton.
